transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. I'm here because... well, for the last couple of years I just feel low all the time. Like, even when I'm at work, or at church, or around people I care about, there's just this heavy, empty feeling. It just doesn't really ever lift.
During these past two years, have there been any periods lasting longer than two months where you felt completely like yourself and your mood was normal?

No, not really. I mean, there might be a day or two here and there where things feel a little lighter, but it never lasts. Definitely not for two months. It's just been a constant... heaviness, pretty much the whole time.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite?

Yeah, I have. Most days I just... skip eating until my shift is almost over, honestly. Nothing really sounds good. Or sometimes I just end up grabbing snacks from the vending machine at work really late, just because I'm so drained. Because of all that, my weight has been up and down quite a bit. It fluctuates enough that my work pants fit completely different from month to month.
How would you describe your energy levels on a day-to-day basis?

Honestly, I'm just exhausted pretty much every day. Even the small stuff takes a lot out of me. Like, just filling out my inspection logs at work, or driving to basketball, or honestly even just washing my hair... it all feels like it takes way more energy than I actually have. And resting on my days off doesn't really help. It doesn't refill me at all, I just stay drained.
How do you feel about yourself, generally speaking?

I don't know, I guess I don't really think about it that much. I just sort of... exist, you know? I wouldn't say I feel great about myself, but I'm not really sure how to describe it beyond that. It's just kind of neutral or... maybe just empty.
Do you find it difficult to focus or make decisions during your daily routine?

No, not really. I mean, my job is basically just checking things and sorting them, so it's pretty repetitive. I just kind of go through the motions. I don't think I've had any real trouble focusing on it or making decisions about it. It's just... it's just what I do.
Do you often find yourself feeling hopeless about the future?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, I don't really think about the future all that much to begin with. I just kind of try to get through each day as it comes. So, no, I don't think I feel hopeless about it... I just don't really picture much of anything when I try to look ahead.
How has your sleep been over the past two years?

It hasn't been very good. I mean, I'll be completely exhausted after standing on the production floor all day, but... when I actually get in bed, my mind just keeps running. I end up thinking about everything I'm behind on. And even if I do manage to fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I barely rested at all. It's pretty much been like that for the whole two years.

During these past two years, have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt significantly worse than your usual baseline, perhaps including a loss of interest or pleasure in almost all of your daily activities?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've felt pretty much the same this whole time. It's just a constant feeling of being down and tired, but it hasn't really spiked or gotten suddenly worse for a couple of weeks like that. It's just... steady, I guess. So, no, nothing like what you're describing.
